You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From e81e36a96bb56f243b5ac1d114c37c086761595b Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Alan Douglas <adouglas@cadence.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Oct 2018 17:15:54 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] PCI: cadence: Write MSI data with 32bits

According to the PCIe specification, although the MSI data is only
16bits, the upper 16bits should be written as 0. Use writel
instead of writew when writing the MSI data to the host.

Fixes: 37dddf14f1ae ("PCI: cadence: Add EndPoint Controller driver for Cadence PCIe controller")
Signed-off-by: Alan Douglas <adouglas@cadence.com>
Signed-off-by: Lorenzo Pieralisi <lorenzo.pieralisi@arm.com>
---
 drivers/pci/controller/pcie-cadence-ep.c | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/drivers/pci/controller/pcie-cadence-ep.c b/drivers/pci/controller/pcie-cadence-ep.c
index 6692654798d4..c3a088910f48 100644
--- a/drivers/pci/controller/pcie-cadence-ep.c
+++ b/drivers/pci/controller/pcie-cadence-ep.c
@@ -355,7 +355,7 @@ static int cdns_pcie_ep_send_msi_irq(struct cdns_pcie_ep *ep, u8 fn,
 		ep->irq_pci_addr = (pci_addr & ~pci_addr_mask);
 		ep->irq_pci_fn = fn;
 	}
-	writew(data, ep->irq_cpu_addr + (pci_addr & pci_addr_mask));
+	writel(data, ep->irq_cpu_addr + (pci_addr & pci_addr_mask));
 
 	return 0;
 }
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by using the `writew` function to write 16 bits of MSI data to the host, which did not account for the PCIe specification requirement that the upper 16 bits should be written as 0. This led to incorrect data being sent, as only the lower 16 bits were written without ensuring the upper bits were cleared. The fix involved changing the function to `writel`, which writes 32 bits, thereby ensuring that the upper 16 bits are set to 0 as required by the specification.

Root cause:
The bug was caused by using the `writew` function to write 16 bits of MSI data to the host, which did not account for the PCIe specification requirement that the upper 16 bits should be written as 0. This led to incorrect data being sent, as only the lower 16 bits were written without ensuring the upper bits were cleared. The fix involved changing the function to `writel`, which writes 32 bits, thereby ensuring that the upper 16 bits are set to 0 as required by the specification.
